content: Atom 2 is the anilide nitrogen and atom 3 the ipso carbon of the fluorophenyl, a non-ring bond - and an aliphatic amide nitrogen is a usable anchor, which I confirmed in the last run. Cutting there discards the para-fluoroaniline, which is doubly wrong for this series: the substituents are para where meta is worth about +0.09, and a fluorine on that central ring measured as a small negative. In its place I attach the meta-substituted benzene carrying an azine with an ethynyl at C4. Ethynyl is the control the C4 scan needs: it is strongly electron-withdrawing and linear like the nitrile, but it has no heteroatom at all, so it adds no hydrogen-bond acceptor and no polar surface. If the nitrile's 0.58 is about withdrawal and shape, ethynyl should match it; if it is about the nitrogen lone pair, ethynyl should fall away. It is also the lightest of the good C4 candidates at about 277 Da, so unlike iodine or trifluoromethyl it could actually win on Phi rather than only inform.
